title: Incorporating admiral
text: workflow inspired portions admiral vignette.
code: ## ```yaml ## meta: ##   ID: ADVS ##   Type: ADAM ##   Description: Create Basic ADVS ##   Priority: 1 ## spec: ##   SDTM_DM: ##     _all: ##       required: true ##   SDTM_VS: ##     _all: ##       required: true ## steps: ##   - output: initial_advs ##     name: admiral::derive_vars_merged ##     params: ##       dataset: SDTM_VS ##       dataset_add: SDTM_DM ##       new_vars: !expr exprs(TRT01A) ##       by_vars: !expr exprs(STUDYID, USUBJID) ##   - output: advs ##     name: dplyr::mutate ##     params: ##       .data: initial_advs ##       PARAMCD: !expr rlang::expr(.data[["VSTESTCD"]]) ##       AVAL: !expr rlang::expr(.data[["VSORRES"]]) ##   - output: advs ##     name: admiral::derive_param_map ##     params: ##       dataset: advs ##       by_vars: !expr exprs(STUDYID, USUBJID, TRT01A, VSDTC, VISIT, VISITNUM, VSTPT, VSTPTNUM) ##       sysbp_code: 'SYSBP' ##       diabp_code: 'DIABP' ##       get_unit_expr: !expr rlang::expr(.data[["VSORRESU"]]) ## ``` ADAM_workflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(   strNames = "ADVS",   strPath = "demo_gsmpharmaverse/workflows/2_SDTM_TO_ADAM/",   strPackage = "workr" ) ADAM <- workr::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = ADAM_workflows, lData = sdtm) map2(ADAM, names(ADAM), function(x,y) arrow::write_parquet(x, paste0("demo_gsmpharmaverse/data/ADAM/",y,".parquet"))

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: simple R data pipeline framework. {workr} provides minimal mental model describing executing step--step workflows. simple workflows can combined configurable data pipelines can automate large tasks.

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: {workr} built solve specific problem: reusable, customizable data pipelines complex clinical trial monitoring. core functions {workr} originally developed part {gsm} framework risk-based quality monitoring (RBQM). {gsm} team developed stable, reusable model generating metrics monitor clinical trials. challenge figuring run metrics across large portfolio. Take 30 studies monthly snapshots, needing 15 metrics computed 5 steps, get 27,000 computations per year. study also slightly different requirements, maintaining individual scripts quickly becomes massive pain. {workr}’s solution: Define workflows , track customizations YAML files, compose larger pipelines. original gsm::RunWorkflow functions developed hours seen stopgap picked “real” pipeline. approach proven surprisingly stable flexible. much ’ve created {workr} started using outside {gsm} pipelines.

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: {workr} workflows list objects typically defined yaml files. workflow following components: Steps functions accept data parameters, producing output gets added shared data list Meta workflow-level configuration accessible steps Spec optional data specification defining expected input data workflow. package provides three core functions running workflows: workr::RunStep() - execute single workflow step workr::RunWorkflow() - execute workflow specification (YAML) workr::RunWorkflows() - run multiple workflows sequence

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: Define workflow YAML: Run R: step workflow: Calls function (specified step$name) Passes parameters params (resolving references lData, meta, literal values) Saves result lData using output name Makes available next step ’s ! chaining steps (even whole workflows) together, can build complex pipelines simple, reusable components.
code: # hello_cars.yaml meta:   ID: hello_cars   col: speed steps:   - name: dplyr::pull      output: speed     params:       df: df       col: col   - name: mean     output: result     params:       lData: speed wf <- yaml::read_yaml("hello_cars.yaml") lData <- list(df = cars)  result <- workr::RunWorkflow(   lWorkflow = wf,   lData = lData )  # result = 15.4 (mean of cars$speed)

title: Workflow Execution Helpers

what: workr::RunProject calls multiple sets of workflows
title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: Last least, sometimes want chain multiple calls workr::RunWorkflows(). workr::RunProject() calls workr::RunWorkflows() every sub-directory (phase) given project directory, sharing one lData object across phases. Key options: strPhases — run subset phases, control order bReturnResult / bKeepInputData — passed RunWorkflows() bRecursive — passed MakeWorkflowList() Phases sorted alphabetically default (use numeric prefixes like 01_, 02_ control order).
code: # Project directory structure: # project/ #   01_mapping/ #     ae.yaml #     lb.yaml #   02_analysis/ #     kri.yaml  results <- workr::RunProject(   strPath = "project",   lData = list(raw_data = my_data) ) # Runs 01_mapping workflows first, then 02_analysis # Outputs from 01_mapping are available as inputs to 02_analysis
